title: How Gemma 4 Could Give DeepSeek Eyes
content:
Open source language models like DeepSeek have billions of neurons, yet they can't process images directly.

In order for them to process images, they have to use a component (called a visual encoder) to translate the pixels into a form that is suitable for them to understand, then use this new form to understand what the image is about.

This implies:

 New Component Needed : We need a separate neural network to process the images.

Time Lag : we need to wait till the image processing stuff is finished to give it to the actual brain to reason.

Training Pipeline : we have to train both the image processing model and the main AI model.

Consumer Hardware unfriendly : we have to fit both the image model and the LLM model, which takes up processing.

What if we could make an architecture change that allows the main LLM to process images without needing any other separate visual processing component? In fact, Gemma 4 does exactly this. This is a model released by Google that allows it to process images directly. And recently, they open sourced the technical details.

Now open source labs can use this to build a better version of models like DeepSeek that have innate multi modal processing capabilities. This is a huge win for open source.

title: Make It Bad. Make It Anyway.
excerpt: A case for making things without chasing perfection.
content:
Artists and creative people need a space to play around without the pressure of external standards telling them what the “right” or “wrong” choice is, allowing themselves to fuck up, learn from it, and move on.

That is, make more “Jank” stuff.

By “Jank,” I mean imperfect art. Art that isn’t trying to prove how skilled we are.

I know that if I spend a lifetime sculpting marble, I could eventually reach Michelangelo-level power mode.

But if I follow that route, to be satisfied, I have to keep practicing, studying, following tutorials, refining my technique, and chasing that level of mastery.

I don’t want that.

There are some things that I want to be good at: scripting and audio storytelling. I feel confident in scripting, and I do have a good mic. Now, the only thing that holds me back is... visuals.

But now, if my goal is to produce “Jank,” I don’t have to worry about making it perfect.

Which means I could just make things and release them, without spending an eternity making them look “right.”

And that would help me realize my goal of just making things.

(His name is Chakkara Kurukkan)
